exercise.name: Glute Bridge March

reference.title: Glute Bridge March
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip extension hold with alternating single-leg support)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you lift into the bridge, breathe steadily while marching, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 0.5 s to lift each knee, a short hold, 0.5 s to set it down

prescription.progression: Longer holds with the knee up, then single-leg glute bridge

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width, arms on the floor by your sides.
Breathe out, press through the heels and lift into a bridge: knees, hips and shoulders in one line.
Keep the hips high and level, lift the right knee until the thigh is vertical, then set the foot back down.
Same on the left: the pelvis must not drop or twist.
Breathe in and roll the hips back down to the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Hips dropping when a foot lifts
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glute of the standing leg harder, or lift the foot only a little.

mistakes.mistake: Pelvis twisting toward the lifted leg
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs and keep both hip bones level, like a tray of water.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to stay up
mistakes.fix: Ribs down; tuck the pelvis slightly.
Slow, deliberate steps with a short pause at the top.

kinematics.norm: Hips extend to neutral at the top (straight knee-hip-shoulder line); no extra lumbar arch (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the top is the traditional bridge; more knee bend shifts work away from the hamstrings (Lehecka 2017)

kinematics.setup: Hip joint 8.6 cm above the floor
kinematics.norm: Pelvis lifts until the line is straight (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Hip 62°, knee 90°; foot 65.4 cm off the floor; pelvis level
kinematics.norm: Free knee rises until the thigh is about vertical while the pelvis stays level (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s per march (0.5 s up, 0.2 s hold, 0.5 s down), 1.4 s down
kinematics.norm: Controlled: about 1 s per march with a brief hold (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #7627, Glute Bridge March (movement reference only)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Electromyographic analysis of core trunk, hip and thigh muscles during 9 rehabilitation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2007; PubMed 18560185)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Low back discomfort: lower the bridge height and brace first.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hips drop when marching: lift the heel only (toe tap) instead of the whole leg.
Hamstring cramps: bring the feet a little closer to the hips.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; their share rises as the feet move away from the hips (Lehecka 2017).

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level, most of all when one foot is off the floor.
